sentences.text: Terminonatator was a genus of elasmosaurid plesiosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous in Saskatchewan, Canada.
As an adult, this creature was small for its group, reaching about 7 meters in length, potentially up to 9 meters if it possessed an extremely long neck.
The preserved skull measures 26.8 cm in length but is broken near the posterior end.
Unlike other plesiosaurs, Terminonatator had a closed pineal foramen and only nine teeth in the premaxillary bones at the snout tip, though this might be individual variation.
Over 150 gastroliths, with the largest measuring 6 cm in diameter, were found within the rib cage.
Tamaki Sato named and described the species Terminonatator ponteixensis in 2003.
Only one species, T. ponteixensis, has been described for this genus.
Terminonatator belongs to the parent group Elasmosaurinae.
Terminonatator is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
Terminonatator is classified as a reptile.
Terminonatator lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
